newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Peres doesn't quit despite party defeat.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peres doesn't quit despite party defeat.

text.p: Former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres said on Wednesday he was not leaving politics despite a stinging slight from his Labour party.

Peres steps down as party leader in June, a year after losing national elections to Benjamin Netanyahu. On Tuesday, Labour rejected a proposal to discuss honouring Peres with the new title of party president to secure his status ahead of a changing of guard.
"I will continue acting," Peres, 73, told Israel radio after the vote. "In what framework, I will consider."
Israeli newspapers hailed "The End of the Peres Era," but the daily Yedioth Ahronoth showed a picture of a somber-faced Peres under a headline saying: "Not quitting, not leaving."

Although twice prime minister, once in a power-sharing deal in the 1980s and a second time as successor to slain Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin in 1995, the Polish-born Peres never won a national election outright in five tries from 1977 to 1996.
Ehud Barak, a former army chief born in Israel in 1942, is expected to succeed Peres as party leader. He told Army radio on Wednesday: "The Labour party yesterday embarked on a new course."
Peres had hoped the position of party president would give him some powers. In rejecting the motion, the party supported a counter-proposal to discuss the matter in September.
By then, however, Barak is expected to be chairman and able to define the role as merely a figurehead. Peres said before Tuesday's vote he would not consider the position at a later date.
A diplomat whose skills made him a welcome visitor throughout the world, Peres long seemed out of place on Israel's political stage.
As foreign minister he and Rabin, then prime minister, shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994 with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for a 1993 deal that gave Palestinians self-rule.
After losing the bid for party president, Peres vowed to continue working for peace but did not spell out his plans.
"I have a title and a role," he told Army radio. "My title is Shimon Peres and my role is to fight for peace."
